title: The Shining
prompt: A continuous low tracking shot follows a child riding a tricycle through a long corridor. Keep a medium-wide rear view with the rider centered, the camera near wheel height, and a steady gap behind the subject. Use a wide field of view to retain the floor, nearby doorframes and distant vanishing point, without prescribing an exact focal length. Match the rider’s measured pace with smooth forward translation and gentle turns; nearby doorframes should pass faster than distant architectural features. Keep focal length fixed. No zoom, overtaking, abrupt acceleration, cuts, exaggerated shake or impossible passage through walls.

title: In the Mood for Love
prompt: A continuous locked-off medium shot observes a person through a narrow doorway from an adjacent room. Place the person off-center inside the visible opening, leaving a dark, softly separated doorframe close to the camera across one side of the image. Use a restrained field of view with readable corridor depth behind the subject; do not prescribe an exact focal length. Let the person move slowly within the opening while the foreground edge partially conceals a shoulder but keeps the face readable. Preserve the near-frame, subject and distant-corridor layers. No camera slide to clear the obstruction, pan, zoom, complete facial occlusion, focus pumping, abrupt movement or cuts.
attribution: CRITERION / YouTube · Three Reasons: In the Mood for Love
